The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim that every irregular optical shortlist can already be resolved by reusing the same flat bombe menu that worked in the first smooth mixed case. What it now does support, however, is a sharper rule for the opposite regime: if the shortlist is already localized, parity-sensitive, or otherwise readout-near, then a trigger-sensitive prefilter should be run before the finer bombe stage. In cryptanalytic language this is closer to a crib- or score-guided sieve than to a blind bombe alone.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First defect/readout-near shortlist case]
\label{def:first-defect-readout-near-shortlist-case}
Assume that an optical shortlist has already been produced and structurally back-read. We say that the shortlist is in the \emph{first defect/readout-near case} if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item the leading mismatch is localized rather than globally smooth across the wavelength window;
  \item at least one parity-sensitive or sign-changing readout feature persists under the first smooth rerun;
  \item the shortlist is no longer well explained by pure smooth offset or pure smooth curvature alone;
  \item the back-reading stage therefore places defect/readout reopening in the admissible first tier instead of postponing it behind only smooth explanations.
\end{enumerate}
In that case the first coarse reopening menu may be written schematically as
\[
\mathcal M_0^{\mathrm{def}}=\{\mu_{\mathrm B},\mu_{\mathrm C},\mu_{\mathrm{BC}},\mu_{\mathrm D},\mu_{\mathrm{BD}},\mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\},
\]
where \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\) denotes a direct defect/readout reopening, while \(\mu_{\mathrm{BD}}\) and \(\mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\) denote mixed readout-plus-smooth repair candidates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Readout-trigger sieve]
\label{def:readout-trigger-sieve}
Assume that the first defect/readout-near shortlist case is present. A \emph{readout-trigger sieve} is the first pre-bombe filter that acts on \(\mathcal M_0^{\mathrm{def}}\) by retaining only those candidates whose predicted local trigger profile remains compatible with the observed irregularity pattern. At the present stage this compatibility is tested only through the following coarse signals:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item locality of the mismatch peak or trough;
  \item persistence of a parity-sensitive or sign-changing feature under smooth rerun;
  \item failure of pure smooth offset-only or curvature-only corrections to absorb the irregularity;
  \item absence of a global residual deterioration after a first local readout patch is inserted.
\end{enumerate}
Candidates failing this trigger profile are removed before the finer structural bombe is run. Thus the sieve is a first score-guided menu compression step for defect/readout-near cases.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[First trigger-sieve-plus-bombe reduction in the defect/readout-near optical case]
\label{prop:first-trigger-sieve-plus-bombe-reduction-in-the-defect-readout-near-optical-case}
Assume that the first defect/readout-near shortlist case of Definition~\ref{def:first-defect-readout-near-shortlist-case} is present and that the readout-trigger sieve of Definition~\ref{def:readout-trigger-sieve} is run before the deeper bombe stage. Assume further that the current residual picture satisfies the following first applied tests:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item after the first smooth rerun, the leading irregularity remains localized and parity-sensitive rather than dissolving into a globally smooth pattern;
  \item pure boundary recalibration \(\mu_{\mathrm B}\), pure carrier refinement \(\mu_{\mathrm C}\), and their smooth mixed version \(\mu_{\mathrm{BC}}\) each leave that localized irregularity structurally visible;
  \item a first direct readout patch candidate \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\) removes the localized trigger without producing a new global offset or curvature drift of leading order;
  \item the hybrid candidates \(\mu_{\mathrm{BD}}\) and \(\mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\) do not improve the local trigger any further than \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\), but do reintroduce a smooth boundary- or carrier-type residue.
\end{enumerate}
Then the two-stage procedure already yields
\[
\mu_{\mathrm B},\ \mu_{\mathrm C},\ \mu_{\mathrm{BC}}
\quad\text{eliminated by the trigger sieve,}
\]
and after the subsequent bombe comparison on the reduced menu
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal M}_0^{\mathrm{def}}=\{\mu_{\mathrm D},\mu_{\mathrm{BD}},\mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\},
\]
one further obtains
\[
\mu_{\mathrm{BD}},\ \mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\quad\text{eliminated,}
\]
so that the surviving coarse reopening branch is
\[
\mu_{\mathrm D}.
\]
Moreover, if one opens beneath \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\) the first finite submenu
\[
\mathcal M_1(\mu_{\mathrm D})=\{\nu_{\mathrm D},\nu_{\mathrm{D\to B}},\nu_{\mathrm{D\to C}}\},
\]
where \(\nu_{\mathrm D}\) means ``keep the defect/readout correction local,'' \(\nu_{\mathrm{D\to B}}\) means ``repair the local trigger and then add a boundary cleanup,'' and \(\nu_{\mathrm{D\to C}}\) means ``repair the local trigger and then add a carrier cleanup,'' and if no leading smooth residue remains after the local repair, then the nested bombe may further eliminate
\[
\nu_{\mathrm{D\to B}},\qquad \nu_{\mathrm{D\to C}},
\]
so that \(\nu_{\mathrm D}\) survives as the first ordered refinement path.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The point is that the defect/readout-near regime is structurally different from the first smooth mixed case. By assumptions~(i) and~(ii), the observed irregularity remains localized and parity-sensitive after the first smooth rerun, so the pure smooth candidates \(\mu_{\mathrm B},\mu_{\mathrm C},\mu_{\mathrm{BC}}\) fail already at the trigger-sieve level: none of them predicts that a localized readout-like cue should persist once the mismatch is rerun through a purely smooth correction class. Hence they may be discarded before the deeper bombe tree is entered.

This leaves only the reduced menu \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_0^{\mathrm{def}}\). By assumption~(iii), the direct readout candidate \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\) removes the very local trigger that motivated the defect/readout reopening and does so without creating a new leading smooth mismatch. Therefore it survives both the sieve and the subsequent bombe test. By assumption~(iv), the hybrid candidates \(\mu_{\mathrm{BD}}\) and \(\mu_{\mathrm{CD}}\) do not buy a better local trigger reduction than \(\mu_{\mathrm D}\) itself, but they do reintroduce smooth boundary- or carrier-type residues. They therefore fail the non-worsening/improvement filter at the bombe stage and are eliminated.

For the nested step, if no leading smooth residue remains after the local readout repair, then adding a second-stage boundary or carrier cleanup is gratuitous at the present depth and so fails the same minimality-without-deterioration logic that underlies the bombe. Hence \(\nu_{\mathrm{D\to B}}\) and \(\nu_{\mathrm{D\to C}}\) are removed, while \(\nu_{\mathrm D}\) survives as the first ordered path. The combined procedure has therefore done genuine work: it first compresses the defect/readout-near menu by a trigger-sensitive sieve and then uses the bombe only on the structurally relevant remainder.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the trigger-sieve-plus-bombe step buys in the first defect/readout-near case]
\label{cor:what-the-trigger-sieve-plus-bombe-step-buys-in-the-first-defect-readout-near-case}
Whenever a later argument in the present v3.24.0 working line reaches the first defect/readout-near shortlist case, it is sufficient to read the gain as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item the wrong smooth candidates are removed before the deeper bombe tree is opened;
  \item defect/readout reopening no longer has to compete on equal footing with smooth candidates that already fail the observed trigger profile;
  \item the bombe is applied only to a reduced menu that is already locally score-filtered;
  \item if the local repair removes the trigger cleanly, the first deeper path may stop at a local readout correction instead of overfitting smooth cleanup layers.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the defect/readout-near regime does not need the same flat bombe as the smooth mixed regime: it benefits from a first sieve and only then from a narrower bombe.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
This is the operational reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:first-trigger-sieve-plus-bombe-reduction-in-the-defect-readout-near-optical-case}. The proposition shows that the correct tool order changes with the optical regime: in the smooth mixed case the bombe acts first, while in the defect/readout-near case a trigger-sensitive sieve should come before the bombe.
\end{proof}




\begin{remark}[Status of the first tensorized tool-readout control layer in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-tensorized-tool-readout-control-layer-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim that the full structural diagnostic workflow has already been turned into a learned global policy. What it now does support, however, is a first minimal tensorized control layer: regime, tool, readout class, and next regime may already be stored in one sparse structural transition tensor whose matrix shadows recover a readable Markov-style surface.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Minimal structural diagnostic transition tensor]
\label{def:minimal-structural-diagnostic-transition-tensor}
Let \(\mathfrak R\) be a finite set of admissible diagnostic regimes, let \(\mathfrak U\) be a finite set of admissible structural tools, and let \(\mathfrak C\) be a finite set of admissible readout classes. A \emph{minimal structural diagnostic transition tensor} is a sparse four-axis tensor
\[
\Theta\in \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^{\mathfrak R\times \mathfrak U\times \mathfrak C\times \mathfrak R},
\qquad
\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}\ge 0,
\]
with the following reading:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item \(r\in\mathfrak R\) is the current diagnostic regime;
  \item \(u\in\mathfrak U\) is the tool applied at the present step;
  \item \(c\in\mathfrak C\) is the currently observed readout class;
  \item \(r'\in\mathfrak R\) is the next regime opened by that tool/readout action.
\end{enumerate}
The tensor is called \emph{admissible} if \(\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}=0\) whenever the pair \((u,c)\) is structurally incompatible with the current regime \(r\) or whenever the resulting next regime \(r'\) violates the already validated closure/transport constraints of the active optical sector.

For the present first v3.24.0 working layer one may read \(\mathfrak R\) schematically through regimes such as
\[
\mathfrak R=\{r_{\mathrm{sm}},r_{\mathrm{dr}},r_{\mathrm{nr}},r_{\mathrm{bt}}\},
\]
where \(r_{\mathrm{sm}}\) denotes a smooth mixed regime, \(r_{\mathrm{dr}}\) a defect/readout-near regime, \(r_{\mathrm{nr}}\) a deeper nested-refinement regime, and \(r_{\mathrm{bt}}\) a backtracking regime. Likewise one may read
\[
\mathfrak U=\{u_{\mathrm B},u_{\mathrm S},u_{\mathrm N},u_{\mathrm R}\},
\]
where \(u_{\mathrm B}\) denotes a bombe step, \(u_{\mathrm S}\) a trigger-sieve step, \(u_{\mathrm N}\) a nested-bombe step, and \(u_{\mathrm R}\) a residual retest.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Markov shadows and tool priority slices of the minimal diagnostic tensor]
\label{prop:markov-shadows-and-tool-priority-slices-of-the-minimal-diagnostic-tensor}
Assume that \(\Theta\) is an admissible minimal structural diagnostic transition tensor in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:minimal-structural-diagnostic-transition-tensor}. Then the following reduced objects are canonically available.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item For every fixed pair \((r,c)\), the slice
  \[
  \Theta_{r,\bullet,c}^{\;\bullet}
  \]
  ranks which tools may legitimately act next and into which regimes they may open.
  \item For every nonnegative weight family \((w_{u,c})_{u,c}\), the contraction
  \[
  M_{r}^{\;r'}=\sum_{u\in\mathfrak U}\sum_{c\in\mathfrak C} w_{u,c}\,\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}
  \]
  defines a Markov-style \emph{regime shadow} on \(\mathfrak R\).
  \item For every fixed pair \((r,c)\), the tool-priority score
  \[
  \Pi_{r,c}(u)=\sum_{r'\in\mathfrak R}\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}
  \]
  measures the admissible structural weight of tool \(u\) under the present regime/readout combination.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the tensor stores the tool/readout dependence as part of the structural layer itself, while ordinary regime-only Markov matrices appear merely as contractions of that richer object.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first statement is immediate from the meaning of the tensor indices: once the current regime \(r\) and readout class \(c\) are fixed, the remaining slice over \(u\) and \(r'\) records which tools are admissible and where they may lead. The second statement is a standard contraction: summing over tools and readout classes with nonnegative weights produces a regime-to-regime matrix that forgets the internal control structure and therefore acts only as a shadow of the full tensor. The third statement simply collects the total admissible outgoing weight of each tool under the fixed pair \((r,c)\). Since inadmissible entries are zero by construction, these scores already encode the structural exclusions. Hence the tensor contains both the richer control information and, by contraction, the simpler Markov-style surface.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First four-axis diagnostic control rule in the current optical line]
\label{cor:first-four-axis-diagnostic-control-rule-in-the-current-optical-line}
Within the present v3.24.0 working line it is sufficient, at first pass, to read the minimal tensor layer as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item in the smooth mixed regime with smooth mixed readout, the dominant admissible slice gives priority to the bombe tool before the nested-bombe or backtracking layers;
  \item in the defect/readout-near regime with localized trigger-bearing readout, the dominant admissible slice gives priority to the trigger sieve before the bombe and nested-bombe layers;
  \item after one surviving local refinement, the next admissible slice may shift priority from the coarse bombe/sieve tools to the nested-bombe or residual-retest tools;
  \item if all local children die, the admissible outgoing weight concentrates on the backtracking regime shadow rather than on deeper forward reopening.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the tool readout is no longer external bookkeeping: it has become part of the minimal structural transition layer itself, and the older regime-only Markov description survives merely as a readable projection.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first two items are exactly the regime split already established above: the smooth mixed case is bombe-first, while the defect/readout-near case is sieve-first. The third item records the fact that after a successful coarse reduction, the next meaningful motion occurs on the deeper nested or residual-testing layer rather than by restarting the same coarse menu. The fourth item is the backtracking clause already built into the nested bombe logic. All four statements therefore follow by reading the corresponding admissible slices of \(\Theta\) and, when desired, contracting them to the appropriate Markov shadow.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Status of the first diagnostic shell condition in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-diagnostic-shell-condition-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} reinterpret the new tool/readout tensor as a physical four-momentum object. What it now does support, however, is one first shell-style restriction on that tensor: only closure-, transport-, readout-, and depth-compatible transitions are allowed to carry nonzero structural weight. In that sense the control layer now has a first four-impulse-like admissibility surface without identifying its axes with physical momentum coordinates.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First diagnostic shell condition for the minimal transition tensor]
\label{def:first-diagnostic-shell-condition-for-the-minimal-transition-tensor}
Let \(\Theta\) be a minimal structural diagnostic transition tensor in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:minimal-structural-diagnostic-transition-tensor}. For every transition tuple
\[
q=(r,u,c,r')\in \mathfrak R\times \mathfrak U\times \mathfrak C\times \mathfrak R
\]
let
\[
\chi_{\mathrm{cl}}(q),\;\chi_{\mathrm{tr}}(q),\;\chi_{\mathrm{ro}}(q),\;\chi_{\mathrm{dp}}(q)\in\{0,1\}
\]
denote the first closure-, transport-, readout-, and depth/backtracking-compatibility indicators, respectively. Here:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item \(\chi_{\mathrm{cl}}(q)=1\) means that the proposed next regime \(r'\) preserves the already validated closure carrier class of the active optical sector;
  \item \(\chi_{\mathrm{tr}}(q)=1\) means that the move from \(r\) to \(r'\) is compatible with the currently admissible transport picture;
  \item \(\chi_{\mathrm{ro}}(q)=1\) means that the tool/readout pair \((u,c)\) is compatible with the observed readout class in regime \(r\);
  \item \(\chi_{\mathrm{dp}}(q)=1\) means that the transition respects the local depth rule, i.e. it either advances by one admissible refinement layer or returns by an admissible backtracking step after child failure.
\end{enumerate}
Define the \emph{diagnostic shell defect} by
\[
\mathfrak s_{\mathrm{diag}}(q)
:=(1-\chi_{\mathrm{cl}}(q))+(1-\chi_{\mathrm{tr}}(q))+(1-\chi_{\mathrm{ro}}(q))+(1-\chi_{\mathrm{dp}}(q)).
\]
We say that \(q\) lies on the \emph{first diagnostic shell} if
\[
\mathfrak s_{\mathrm{diag}}(q)=0.
\]
The tensor \(\Theta\) is called \emph{shell-admissible} if
\[
\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathfrak s_{\mathrm{diag}}(r,u,c,r')=0.
\]
Thus the support of \(\Theta\) is contained in the shell of fully compatible diagnostic transitions.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Shell support and vanishing off-shell shadows of the minimal diagnostic tensor]
\label{prop:shell-support-and-vanishing-off-shell-shadows-of-the-minimal-diagnostic-tensor}
Assume that \(\Theta\) is shell-admissible in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:first-diagnostic-shell-condition-for-the-minimal-transition-tensor}. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item If a transition tuple \(q=(r,u,c,r')\) is off shell, i.e. \(\mathfrak s_{\mathrm{diag}}(q)>0\), then
  \[
  \Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}=0.
  \]
  \item For every fixed pair \((r,c)\), if a tool \(u\) is off shell against every possible next regime \(r'\), then its priority score vanishes:
  \[
  \Pi_{r,c}(u)=\sum_{r'\in\mathfrak R}\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}=0.
  \]
  \item For every nonnegative weight family \((w_{u,c})\), the regime shadow
  \[
  M_r^{\;r'}=\sum_{u\in\mathfrak U}\sum_{c\in\mathfrak C} w_{u,c}\,\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}
  \]
  vanishes whenever no shell-admissible tool/readout tuple connects \(r\) to \(r'\).
  \item Consequently the readable Markov-shadow surface is not free-standing: it is supported only on the shell-projection of the richer tensor layer.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Item~(i) is the definition of shell-admissibility. Item~(ii) follows immediately by summing only zero entries when the chosen tool is off shell for the fixed pair \((r,c)\). Item~(iii) is the same observation after contraction: if every contributing tuple is off shell, then every summand in the weighted shadow matrix vanishes. Item~(iv) is therefore only the conceptual restatement that the regime-only Markov picture inherits its support from the shell-restricted tensor and cannot generate additional transitions by itself.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First shell reading of the current optical control layer]
\label{cor:first-shell-reading-of-the-current-optical-control-layer}
Within the present v3.24.0 working line it is sufficient, at first pass, to read the diagnostic shell as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item in the first smooth mixed regime with smooth mixed readout, the bombe-first slice lies on shell, while a trigger-sieve-first move or a gratuitous immediate defect/readout detour is off shell at the same depth;
  \item in the first defect/readout-near regime with localized trigger-bearing readout, the trigger-sieve-first slice lies on shell, while purely smooth reruns that leave the trigger profile structurally untouched are off shell;
  \item after one surviving coarse reduction, forward motion stays on shell only through an admissible nested or residual-retest step;
  \item if all local children die, the forward shell closes and only the admissible backtracking return remains on shell.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the current tensorized control layer already has one first shell geometry: not every formally writable next step lies on the admissible surface, and the visible Markov shadow inherits exactly that restriction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The first item is the shell reformulation of the already established bombe-first rule for the smooth mixed case. The second item is the shell reformulation of the sieve-first rule for the defect/readout-near case. The third item records that after one surviving coarse reduction the next admissible step occurs on the nested or residual-testing layer rather than by arbitrarily restarting the coarse menu. The fourth item is the backtracking clause already built into the nested bombe logic: once every child fails, deeper forward motion leaves the admissible depth rule and falls off shell, so only return remains. Hence the current optical control layer may indeed be read through one first diagnostic shell condition.
\end{proof}


\begin{remark}[Status of the first explicit shell-supported mini-assignment in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-explicit-shell-supported-mini-assignment-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim that the whole diagnostic tensor has already been filled by data or by a complete learned policy. What it now does support, however, is one first explicit mini-assignment on the shell for the two leading optical regimes already treated above. This gives a concrete local support picture rather than only an abstract existence statement.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First explicit mini-assignment for the leading optical regimes]
\label{def:first-explicit-mini-assignment-for-the-leading-optical-regimes}
Let
\[
\mathfrak R_\ast=\{r_{\mathrm{sm}},r_{\mathrm{dr}},r_{\mathrm{nr}},r_{\mathrm{bt}}\},
\qquad
\mathfrak U_\ast=\{u_{\mathrm B},u_{\mathrm S},u_{\mathrm N},u_{\mathrm R}\},
\qquad
\mathfrak C_\ast=\{c_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{tr}}\}
\]
be the reduced regime, tool, and readout sets where:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item $r_{\mathrm{sm}}$ denotes the first smooth mixed regime, $r_{\mathrm{dr}}$ the first defect/readout-near regime, $r_{\mathrm{nr}}$ a surviving nested-refinement regime, and $r_{\mathrm{bt}}$ a backtracking regime;
  \item $u_{\mathrm B}$ denotes the bombe, $u_{\mathrm S}$ the trigger sieve, $u_{\mathrm N}$ the nested bombe, and $u_{\mathrm R}$ the residual retest;
  \item $c_{\mathrm{sm}}$ denotes the smooth mixed readout class and $c_{\mathrm{tr}}$ the localized trigger-bearing readout class.
\end{enumerate}
Fix positive weights $a,b>0$. The \emph{first explicit mini-assignment} is the shell-admissible tensor support rule
\[
\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}=0
\quad\text{for all tuples except}
\quad
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{sm}},u_{\mathrm B},c_{\mathrm{sm}}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{nr}}}=a,
\qquad
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{dr}},u_{\mathrm S},c_{\mathrm{tr}}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{nr}}}=b.
\]
Thus the first smooth mixed regime supports only the bombe-first move into the next nested-refinement layer, while the first defect/readout-near regime supports only the sieve-first move into that same next layer.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Priority readout of the first explicit mini-assignment]
\label{prop:priority-readout-of-the-first-explicit-mini-assignment}
Assume the mini-assignment of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-mini-assignment-for-the-leading-optical-regimes}. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item In the smooth mixed regime with smooth mixed readout,
  \[
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{sm}}}(u_{\mathrm B})=a>0,
  \qquad
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{sm}}}(u)=0
  \quad\text{for every }u\neq u_{\mathrm B}.
  \]
  \item In the defect/readout-near regime with localized trigger-bearing readout,
  \[
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{tr}}}(u_{\mathrm S})=b>0,
  \qquad
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{tr}}}(u)=0
  \quad\text{for every }u\neq u_{\mathrm S}.
  \]
  \item The corresponding regime shadow has only the two nonzero entries
  \[
  M_{r_{\mathrm{sm}}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{nr}}}>0,
  \qquad
  M_{r_{\mathrm{dr}}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{nr}}}>0,
  \]
  and every competing first step from these two leading regimes vanishes in the shadow because it is off shell in the current mini-assignment.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the first move is uniquely selected in both leading regimes once the regime/readout class has already been identified.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By construction the only nonzero tensor entry above $(r_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{sm}})$ is the bombe entry with weight $a$, so the corresponding priority score is $a$ and every competing tool score is a sum of zeros. The same argument gives the unique trigger-sieve score $b$ above $(r_{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{tr}})$. Contracting the tensor over tools and readout classes yields exactly the stated two nonzero shadow transitions, because there are no further admissible support points in the reduced assignment. The uniqueness claim is therefore immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the explicit mini-assignment already buys for proof economy]
\label{cor:what-the-explicit-mini-assignment-already-buys-for-proof-economy}
Whenever a later argument in the present v3.24.0 working line has already established one of the two leading regime/readout pairs
\[
(r_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{sm}})
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
(r_{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{tr}}),
\]
it is no longer necessary to reopen the whole first-step tool menu by hand. It is sufficient to cite the support of the mini-assignment and conclude immediately:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item smooth mixed $\Rightarrow$ bombe-first;
  \item defect/readout-near $\Rightarrow$ sieve-first;
  \item every competing first move is already excluded on shell;
  \item the remaining proof burden begins only at the next nested-refinement or residual-testing stage.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the new tensor layer does \emph{not} prove the whole structural chain by itself, but it does shorten repeated local admissibility arguments by packaging the first tool choice into a shell-supported support statement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The statement is the direct reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:priority-readout-of-the-first-explicit-mini-assignment}. Once the active regime/readout pair is known, the support of the mini-assignment already kills the competing first-step tools. Therefore the proof no longer needs a separate fresh elimination argument for that first move and may start directly at the surviving next layer. What remains to be shown is still substantial --- namely that the chosen regime/readout classification was correct and that the downstream refinement actually improves or closes the residual picture --- but the first branching point has been canonically compressed.
\end{proof}


\begin{remark}[Status of the first explicit nested submenu mini-assignment in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-explicit-nested-submenu-mini-assignment-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim that every later nested branch is already fixed by one universal policy. What it now does support, however, is one first explicit submenu assignment on the nested layer immediately below the two leading first-step entries. This turns the second decision point into another shell-supported local support statement rather than leaving it completely informal.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First explicit nested submenu assignment after the two leading entries]
\label{def:first-explicit-nested-submenu-assignment-after-the-two-leading-entries}
Let
\[
\mathfrak R_{\ast\ast}
=
\{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},r_{\partial},r_{\lambda},r_{\mathrm{bt}}\},
\qquad
\mathfrak U_{\ast\ast}
=
\{u_{\partial},u_{\kappa},u_{\lambda},u_{\mathrm{bt}}\},
\qquad
\mathfrak C_{\ast\ast}
=
\{c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa},c_{\mathrm{lt}},c_{\dagger}\}
\]
be the reduced nested regime, tool, and readout sets where:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item $r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}}$ denotes the nested refinement regime entered after the smooth mixed bombe-first step, while $r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}}$ denotes the nested refinement regime entered after the defect/readout-near sieve-first step;
  \item $r_{\partial}$ denotes the next regime after a boundary-offset repair, $r_{\lambda}$ the next regime after a local defect/readout repair, and $r_{\mathrm{bt}}$ the backtracking regime;
  \item $u_{\partial}$ denotes the boundary-offset repair tool, $u_{\kappa}$ a direct carrier-curvature refinement, $u_{\lambda}$ a local defect/readout repair, and $u_{\mathrm{bt}}$ the backtracking tool;
  \item $c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}$ denotes the nested smooth mixed residual class that still reads ``boundary before carrier'', $c_{\mathrm{lt}}$ the persistent localized-trigger class, and $c_{\dagger}$ the dead-child class indicating that the currently opened local submenu has no surviving forward child.
\end{enumerate}
Fix positive weights $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta>0$. The \emph{first explicit nested submenu assignment} is the shell-admissible support rule
\[
\Theta_{r,u,c}^{\;r'}=0
\quad\text{for all tuples except}
\]
\[
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},u_{\partial},c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}}^{\;r_{\partial}}=\alpha,
\qquad
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},u_{\lambda},c_{\mathrm{lt}}}^{\;r_{\lambda}}=\beta,
\]
\[
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},u_{\mathrm{bt}},c_{\dagger}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{bt}}}=\gamma,
\qquad
\Theta_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},u_{\mathrm{bt}},c_{\dagger}}^{\;r_{\mathrm{bt}}}=\delta.
\]
Thus the nested smooth mixed submenu selects boundary-offset repair before a direct carrier move, the nested defect/readout submenu selects local defect/readout repair, and a dead-child readout closes forward motion in favour of backtracking.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Second-step priority readout of the first nested submenu assignment]
\label{prop:second-step-priority-readout-of-the-first-nested-submenu-assignment}
Assume the nested submenu assignment of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-nested-submenu-assignment-after-the-two-leading-entries}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item in the nested smooth mixed regime with readout class $c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}$,
  \[
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}}(u_{\partial})=\alpha>0,
  \qquad
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}}(u)=0
  \quad\text{for every }u\neq u_{\partial};
  \]
  in particular the direct carrier-curvature tool $u_{\kappa}$ is off shell at that second decision point;
  \item in the nested defect/readout regime with readout class $c_{\mathrm{lt}}$,
  \[
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{lt}}}(u_{\lambda})=\beta>0,
  \qquad
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{lt}}}(u)=0
  \quad\text{for every }u\neq u_{\lambda};
  \]
  \item in either nested regime with dead-child readout class $c_{\dagger}$,
  \[
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\dagger}}(u_{\mathrm{bt}})=\gamma>0,
  \qquad
  \Pi_{r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\dagger}}(u_{\mathrm{bt}})=\delta>0,
  \]
  while every competing forward tool has zero score;
  \item the corresponding regime shadow has nonzero support only on the transitions
  \[
  r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}}\to r_{\partial},
  \qquad
  r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}}\to r_{\lambda},
  \qquad
  r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}}\to r_{\mathrm{bt}},
  \qquad
  r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}}\to r_{\mathrm{bt}},
  \]
  under the associated readout classes.
\end{enumerate}
Hence one first second-step priority law is already visible: after the leading first-step selection, the next local move is again uniquely selected once the nested readout class is known.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By construction, above the pair $(r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa})$ the only nonzero support point is the boundary-offset tool with weight $\alpha$, so every competing tool --- including the direct carrier-curvature move --- has priority score zero there. The same reasoning gives the unique local defect/readout repair score $\beta$ above $(r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{lt}})$. For the dead-child class $c_{\dagger}$ the only supported entries are the two backtracking moves with weights $\gamma$ and $\delta$, so every forward continuation vanishes. Contracting over tools and readout classes yields exactly the listed shadow transitions and no others. Therefore the second decision point is again canonically compressed by the support of the assignment.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first nested submenu assignment already buys for proof compression]
\label{cor:what-the-first-nested-submenu-assignment-already-buys-for-proof-compression}
Suppose a later argument in the present v3.24.0 working line has already passed through one of the two leading first-step entries and has reached the associated nested regime. Then it is no longer necessary to reopen the whole second-step submenu by hand whenever one of the following nested readout classes has already been identified:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item $c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa}$ in the smooth mixed nested regime $\Rightarrow$ boundary-offset repair first;
  \item $c_{\mathrm{lt}}$ in the defect/readout nested regime $\Rightarrow$ local defect/readout repair first;
  \item $c_{\dagger}$ in either nested regime $\Rightarrow$ backtracking first.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the current tensor layer now compresses \emph{two} consecutive branching points:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item the first tool choice at the leading optical regimes;
  \item the first nested submenu choice immediately below those leading entries.
\end{enumerate}
What remains open is still substantial --- especially the correctness of the nested readout classification and the downstream residual improvement --- but the proof no longer needs to rebuild the second submenu admissibility argument from scratch each time.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The statement is the direct reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:second-step-priority-readout-of-the-first-nested-submenu-assignment}. Once the relevant nested readout class is known, the support of the nested submenu assignment already kills the competing local tools at the second decision point. Therefore the proof can move directly to the downstream correction or backtracking layer instead of replaying the full submenu elimination. Together with Corollary~\ref{cor:what-the-explicit-mini-assignment-already-buys-for-proof-economy}, this shows that the first two branching points may already be cited as shell-supported support statements.
\end{proof}



\begin{remark}[Status of the first branch-depth policy abstraction in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-branch-depth-policy-abstraction-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim one complete global policy for every possible later diagnostic depth. What it now does support, however, is one first shell-supported \emph{branch-depth policy abstraction} for the early optical control line. The gain is that the two explicit local mini-assignments above may now be read together as one reusable early-depth rule instead of as two disconnected local gadgets.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First shell-supported branch-depth policy]
\label{def:first-shell-supported-branch-depth-policy}
Let
\[
\mathfrak D_\ast=\{0,1\}
\]
be the current early diagnostic depth set, where depth~$0$ denotes the first coarse reopening step and depth~$1$ the first nested submenu step below a surviving coarse child. Using the reduced regime/readout families already fixed in Definitions~\ref{def:first-explicit-mini-assignment-for-the-leading-optical-regimes} and~\ref{def:first-explicit-nested-submenu-assignment-after-the-two-leading-entries}, define the \emph{first shell-supported branch-depth policy}
\[
\mathcal P_\ast : \mathfrak D_\ast \times \mathfrak R \times \mathfrak C \to \mathcal P(\mathfrak U\times \mathfrak R)
\]
by the following nonempty values:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item
  \[
  \mathcal P_\ast(0,r_{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\mathrm{sm}})=\{(u_{\mathrm B},r_{\mathrm{nr}})\};
  \]
  \item
  \[
  \mathcal P_\ast(0,r_{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{tr}})=\{(u_{\mathrm S},r_{\mathrm{nr}})\};
  \]
  \item
  \[
  \mathcal P_\ast(1,r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\partial\!\prec\!\kappa})=\{(u_{\partial},r_{\partial})\};
  \]
  \item
  \[
  \mathcal P_\ast(1,r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\mathrm{lt}})=\{(u_{\lambda},r_{\lambda})\};
  \]
  \item
  \[
  \mathcal P_\ast(1,r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{sm}},c_{\dagger})=\{(u_{\mathrm{bt}},r_{\mathrm{bt}})\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal P_\ast(1,r_{\mathrm{nr}}^{\mathrm{dr}},c_{\dagger})=\{(u_{\mathrm{bt}},r_{\mathrm{bt}})\}.
  \]
\end{enumerate}
For every other triple $(d,r,c)$ at the present stage, $\mathcal P_\ast(d,r,c)$ is left empty or deferred. The policy is called \emph{shell-supported} if every listed pair $(u,r')\in\mathcal P_\ast(d,r,c)$ corresponds to a nonzero shell-admissible tensor support point and every competing pair at the same depth is off shell.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Early-depth support propagation under the first branch-depth policy]
\label{prop:early-depth-support-propagation-under-the-first-branch-depth-policy}
Assume the first explicit mini-assignment of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-mini-assignment-for-the-leading-optical-regimes} and the first nested submenu assignment of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-nested-submenu-assignment-after-the-two-leading-entries}. Then the first shell-supported branch-depth policy of Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-supported-branch-depth-policy} is valid on depths $0$ and $1$, and the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item For every admissible triple $(0,r,c)$ among the two leading coarse entries, the policy returns exactly one surviving next pair $(u,r')$, and every competing first-step move is off shell.
  \item For every admissible triple $(1,r,c)$ among the three currently stabilized nested readout classes, the policy again returns exactly one surviving next pair $(u,r')$, and every competing second-step move is off shell.
  \item Consequently every diagnostic path that stays within the current early-depth window $\mathfrak D_\ast=\{0,1\}$ is uniquely determined, step by step, by the active depth and readout-classified regime pair.
  \item In particular no later proof segment restricted to these two early depths needs to reopen a full sibling menu once the relevant classified triple $(d,r,c)$ has been established.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the current optical control line already carries one finite-depth policy surface: the first two branching levels may be cited as a shell-supported staged control rule rather than replayed as fresh eliminations each time.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
At depth~$0$, the claim is exactly Proposition~\ref{prop:priority-readout-of-the-first-explicit-mini-assignment}: the smooth mixed and defect/readout-near leading pairs admit only the bombe-first and sieve-first support points respectively. At depth~$1$, the claim is exactly Proposition~\ref{prop:second-step-priority-readout-of-the-first-nested-submenu-assignment}: the nested smooth mixed, nested defect/readout, and dead-child readout classes admit only the boundary-offset, local defect/readout, and backtracking moves respectively. Therefore each nonempty policy value listed in Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-supported-branch-depth-policy} is supported by a nonzero shell-admissible tensor entry, while every competing move at the same depth vanishes. The uniqueness of admissible early-depth paths follows by reading the appropriate supported singleton at each stage. Hence any later proof segment that stays inside the current depth window may cite the policy directly instead of rebuilding the corresponding local elimination tree.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first branch-depth policy already buys for proof staging]
\label{cor:what-the-first-branch-depth-policy-already-buys-for-proof-staging}
Suppose a later argument in the present v3.24.0 working line remains inside the currently stabilized early-depth window $\mathfrak D_\ast=\{0,1\}$. Then the proof may be staged in the following compressed form:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item identify the active depth $d\in\{0,1\}$;
  \item classify the active regime/readout pair $(r,c)$;
  \item cite the branch-depth policy $\mathcal P_\ast(d,r,c)$ to obtain the unique admissible next move;
  \item reopen detailed elimination only when the path leaves the present early-depth window or when the relevant readout class has not yet been stabilized.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the current tensorized control layer has now progressed from two isolated local shortcuts to one reusable \emph{proof-staging surface} for the first two branching depths. This does not close the whole proof, but it does compress repeated admissibility work at exactly the place where branching would otherwise bloat the argument most quickly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Items~(i)--(iii) are the direct operational reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:early-depth-support-propagation-under-the-first-branch-depth-policy}. Once depth and regime/readout class are known, the policy returns the unique shell-supported move and all siblings at that same decision point are already excluded. Therefore detailed elimination needs to be reopened only beyond the currently stabilized early-depth window or before the classification itself has been justified. The final sentence is the conceptual summary: the first two branching depths have become one reusable proof-staging surface.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Status of the first shell-compatible local utility layer in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-shell-compatible-local-utility-layer-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim one globally trained diagnostic controller or a complete numerical learning layer. What it now does support, however, is one first \emph{shell-compatible local utility layer} attached to the early branch-depth policy. The gain is that later extensions no longer need to start by postulating a new menu ordering by hand: within the admissible shell, candidate moves may now be ranked by one explicit local score before a deeper explicit mini-assignment has been stabilized.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First shell-compatible local utility functional]
\label{def:first-shell-compatible-local-utility-functional}
Let $(d,r,c)\in \mathfrak D_\ast\times \mathfrak R\times \mathfrak C$ be an early-depth diagnostic triple and let $(u,r')\in \mathfrak U\times \mathfrak R$ be a candidate next move. Assume that with every such candidate one associates the following local diagnostic indicators:
\begin{align*}
\Delta_{\rho}(d,r,c;u,r')&\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0} &&\text{(expected residual reduction)},\\
\Gamma_{\mathrm{cl}}(d,r,c;u,r')&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{(closure compatibility flag)},\\
\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}(d,r,c;u,r')&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{(transport compatibility flag)},\\
\Gamma_{\mathrm{ro}}(d,r,c;u,r')&\in\{0,1\} &&\text{(readout fidelity flag)},\\
K_{\mathrm{bt}}(d,r,c;u,r')&\in\mathbb R_{\ge 0} &&\text{(backtracking or reopening cost)}.
\end{align*}
Choose fixed nonnegative weights
\[
\alpha_{\rho},\alpha_{\mathrm{cl}},\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}},\alpha_{\mathrm{ro}},\alpha_{\mathrm{bt}}\ge 0
\]
with at least one of $\alpha_{\rho},\alpha_{\mathrm{cl}},\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}},\alpha_{\mathrm{ro}}$ strictly positive. The \emph{first shell-compatible local utility functional} is the map
\[
\mathcal U_\ast : \mathfrak D_\ast\times \mathfrak R\times \mathfrak C\times \mathfrak U\times \mathfrak R \to \mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}
\]
defined by
\[
\mathcal U_\ast(d,r,c;u,r')=
\begin{cases}
\alpha_{\rho}\Delta_{\rho}+\alpha_{\mathrm{cl}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cl}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{ro}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{ro}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{bt}}K_{\mathrm{bt}}, & \text{if } (u,r') \text{ is on shell at } (d,r,c),\\[0.4em]
-\infty, & \text{if } (u,r') \text{ is off shell at } (d,r,c).
\end{cases}
\]
Here every symbol on the first line is evaluated at the same quintuple $(d,r,c;u,r')$. The associated \emph{utility-priority correspondence} is
\[
\Pi_\ast(d,r,c)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{(u,r')\in\mathfrak U\times\mathfrak R}\mathcal U_\ast(d,r,c;u,r').
\]
Thus off-shell moves are excluded automatically, while on-shell moves may be ordered by their local residual gain, structural fidelity, and anticipated reopening cost.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Utility refinement of the early branch-depth policy]
\label{prop:utility-refinement-of-the-early-branch-depth-policy}
Assume the first shell-supported branch-depth policy of Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-supported-branch-depth-policy} together with the shell-supported singleton structure established in Proposition~\ref{prop:early-depth-support-propagation-under-the-first-branch-depth-policy}. Then for every currently stabilized early-depth triple $(d,r,c)$ with nonempty policy value, the utility-priority correspondence satisfies
\[
\Pi_\ast(d,r,c)=\mathcal P_\ast(d,r,c).
\]
In particular the first shell-compatible local utility layer does not alter the already stabilized early control surface; it refines it by turning that surface into a scored selection rule. More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item for the two currently stabilized depth-$0$ entries, the unique utility maximizers are the bombe-first and sieve-first moves respectively;
  \item for the three currently stabilized depth-$1$ entries, the unique utility maximizers are the boundary-offset, local defect/readout, and backtracking moves respectively;
  \item every competing sibling move at the same currently stabilized triple has utility $-\infty$ because it is off shell;
  \item therefore the utility layer is immediately compatible with the current proof-staging surface and may be used as the ranking principle for future later-depth extensions before a complete explicit submenu assignment has been frozen.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For every currently stabilized triple $(d,r,c)$, Proposition~\ref{prop:early-depth-support-propagation-under-the-first-branch-depth-policy} says that exactly one admissible next pair $(u,r')$ survives on shell and every sibling at the same decision point is off shell. By Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-compatible-local-utility-functional}, each off-shell sibling therefore receives utility $-\infty$. The unique surviving on-shell pair receives a finite score because all indicator terms are finite and the corresponding shell flags are admissible. Hence the argmax set contains exactly that surviving pair and coincides with the singleton returned by $\mathcal P_\ast(d,r,c)$. The concrete identifications at depths $0$ and $1$ are then just the already stabilized singleton values of the policy: bombe-first and sieve-first on the two coarse leading entries, boundary-offset, local defect/readout, and backtracking on the three currently stabilized nested entries. The final claim is the conceptual reading: once later depths cease to be singleton-supported at first pass, the same utility functional may still rank the remaining on-shell menu before a later explicit assignment has been proved.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first local utility layer already buys for later depth extension]
\label{cor:what-the-first-local-utility-layer-already-buys-for-later-depth-extension}
Suppose a later extension of the present v3.24.0 working line reaches a new diagnostic depth where more than one candidate move remains on shell after the initial admissibility test. Then the proof no longer needs to choose the next move by an entirely ad hoc narrative tie-break. Instead it may proceed in the following order:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item classify the active triple $(d,r,c)$ and restrict to the shell-admissible local menu;
  \item evaluate or estimate the local indicators entering $\mathcal U_\ast$ on that reduced menu;
  \item use $\Pi_\ast(d,r,c)$ as the first scored priority surface inside the admissible shell;
  \item freeze a new explicit submenu assignment only after repeated use or further structural proof has shown that one ranked pattern is stable enough to deserve a hard-coded singleton rule.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the current control architecture now has a natural intermediate layer between pure admissibility and future deeper explicit policies: shell first, utility second, hard-coded submenu only when the ranked pattern has become structurally stable.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The statement is the operational reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:utility-refinement-of-the-early-branch-depth-policy}. On the currently stabilized depths the utility layer reproduces the already known singleton choices exactly, so it is compatible with every argument that already cites the branch-depth policy. At a later depth with several surviving on-shell siblings, the same functional still provides an ordered local surface before a future explicit singleton assignment has been justified. This yields a disciplined extension rule: admissibility cuts the menu first, local utility orders what remains, and only sufficiently persistent ranked patterns are later frozen into a new explicit submenu policy.
\end{proof}


\begin{remark}[Status of the first utility-guided provisional depth-2 continuation layer in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-continuation-layer-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim one complete explicit third-level submenu theorem. What it now does support, however, is one first \emph{utility-guided provisional depth-2 continuation layer}. The gain is that the first step beyond the currently stabilized early-depth window no longer has to reopen a full bespoke elimination tree immediately: once a depth-$2$ local menu is known, the same shell-first/utility-second logic already gives a disciplined continuation rule.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First utility-guided provisional depth-2 continuation rule]
\label{def:first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-continuation-rule}
Let
\[
\mathfrak D_{\bullet}=\{0,1,2\}
\]
be the first extended depth window, and let
\[
\mathfrak H_2\subseteq \mathfrak R\times\mathfrak C\times\mathfrak R\times\mathfrak C
\]
be the set of inherited depth-$2$ parent histories
\[
h=(r_0,c_0,r_1,c_1)
\]
that arise from following the current shell-supported branch-depth policy through depths $0$ and $1$. For such a history $h\in\mathfrak H_2$ and a current depth-$2$ readout class $c_2\in\mathfrak C$, let
\[
\mathcal M_2(h,c_2)\subseteq \mathfrak U\times\mathfrak R
\]
be the shell-admissible local depth-$2$ continuation menu. Using the same indicator package as in Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-compatible-local-utility-functional}, extended to depth $2$, define the \emph{depth-$2$ local utility}
\[
\mathcal U_2(h,c_2;u,r')\in \mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}
\]
by the same shell-first rule:
\[
\mathcal U_2(h,c_2;u,r')=
\begin{cases}
\alpha_{\rho}\Delta_{\rho}+\alpha_{\mathrm{cl}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{cl}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{tr}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{tr}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{ro}}\Gamma_{\mathrm{ro}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{bt}}K_{\mathrm{bt}}, & \text{if } (u,r')\in \mathcal M_2(h,c_2),\\[0.4em]
-\infty, & \text{if } (u,r')\notin \mathcal M_2(h,c_2),
\end{cases}
\]
where every indicator on the first line is evaluated at the same quintuple $(2,h,c_2;u,r')$. The associated \emph{provisional depth-$2$ priority correspondence} is
\[
\Pi_2(h,c_2)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{(u,r')\in \mathfrak U\times\mathfrak R}\mathcal U_2(h,c_2;u,r').
\]
Whenever this argmax is a singleton, the corresponding map
\[
\mathcal P^{\mathrm{prov}}_2(h,c_2)=\Pi_2(h,c_2)
\]
is called the \emph{first utility-guided provisional depth-$2$ continuation rule}. Thus depth $2$ is not yet hard-coded globally, but it is already constrained by shell admissibility and ranked by the same local utility logic as the stabilized early-depth surface.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Utility-supported continuation beyond the stabilized early-depth window]
\label{prop:utility-supported-continuation-beyond-the-stabilized-early-depth-window}
Assume the first shell-supported branch-depth policy of Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-supported-branch-depth-policy} and the local utility layer of Definition~\ref{def:first-shell-compatible-local-utility-functional}. Let a diagnostic path follow that policy through depths $0$ and $1$, thereby producing an inherited history $h\in\mathfrak H_2$. Then the following statements hold for every current depth-$2$ readout class $c_2\in\mathfrak C$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item Every off-shell third-step candidate $(u,r')\notin \mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$ has utility $-\infty$ under $\mathcal U_2(h,c_2;\cdot,\cdot)$.
  \item Every admissible third-step candidate lies in the finite reduced menu $\mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$ and is therefore compared only against other shell-admissible siblings with the same inherited history and current readout class.
  \item If one admissible third-step candidate $(u_{\max},r'_{\max})\in \mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$ strictly dominates all other admissible siblings in local utility, then
  \[
  \Pi_2(h,c_2)=\{(u_{\max},r'_{\max})\}
  \]
  and the provisional depth-$2$ continuation rule is uniquely defined at $(h,c_2)$ without requiring a full new explicit submenu theorem.
  \item Only after such singleton outcomes persist across repeated use or further structural proof should they be frozen into a later hard-coded depth-$2$ submenu policy.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the first extension beyond the stabilized early-depth window may already be staged by the same three-level logic as before: inherited path first, shell admissibility second, local utility third.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Items~(i) and~(ii) are immediate from Definition~\ref{def:first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-continuation-rule}: by construction, $\mathcal U_2$ assigns $-\infty$ to every candidate outside the shell-admissible reduced depth-$2$ menu and finite scores only on the remaining admissible siblings. Therefore no depth-$2$ comparison needs to reopen candidates outside $\mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$. Item~(iii) is then just the defining property of the argmax set: if one admissible sibling has strictly larger utility than every other admissible sibling, the argmax is a singleton and yields a unique provisional continuation rule at $(h,c_2)$. Item~(iv) is the policy reading already encoded in Corollary~\ref{cor:what-the-first-local-utility-layer-already-buys-for-later-depth-extension}: explicit hard-coding should only be performed after repeated structural stabilization, not at the first provisional ranked occurrence. The final sentence summarizes the resulting staged extension principle.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first utility-guided provisional depth-2 layer already buys for proof control]
\label{cor:what-the-first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-layer-already-buys-for-proof-control}
Suppose a proof segment in the present v3.24.0 working line has already followed the current branch-depth policy through depths $0$ and $1$ and now reaches a genuine depth-$2$ menu. Then the proof no longer needs to explode immediately into a bespoke third-level contradiction tree. Instead it may proceed as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item record the inherited history $h\in\mathfrak H_2$ coming from the already stabilized earlier depths;
  \item restrict the third-step menu to the shell-admissible set $\mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$;
  \item rank the surviving siblings by the provisional utility correspondence $\Pi_2(h,c_2)$;
  \item continue directly with the unique maximizer when that maximizer is strict, and otherwise keep only the finite utility-ranked shortlist for any later bombe/backtracking or explicit submenu hardening step.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the first unstabilized depth beyond the current early-depth surface is already proof-manageable: it no longer reopens the full global search space, but only a shell-filtered, utility-ranked local menu inheriting the earlier staged path.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The statement is the direct operational reading of Proposition~\ref{prop:utility-supported-continuation-beyond-the-stabilized-early-depth-window}. The already stabilized earlier depths determine the inherited history $h$, so the depth-$2$ step starts from a path-conditioned local situation rather than from a fresh global menu. Shell admissibility then cuts away all candidates outside $\mathcal M_2(h,c_2)$, while the provisional depth-$2$ utility ranking orders the remaining siblings. If the maximizer is strict, the proof obtains an immediate provisional next move; if not, it still reduces the continuation problem to a small ranked shortlist rather than an uncontrolled branch explosion. This is exactly the promised proof-control gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[First explicit smooth-mixed depth-2 test case]

h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2=(r^{\mathrm{sm}}_0,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_0,r^{\mathrm{sm}}_1,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_1)\in \mathfrak H_2
\]
be the inherited depth-$2$ history produced by the currently stabilized smooth mixed lead path, namely:

  \item at depth $0$ the smooth mixed optical lead case enters the mixed reopening line through the bombe-first choice already fixed by the current early-depth policy;
  \item at depth $1$ the same line chooses boundary-offset repair first, in the sense of the explicit nested submenu assignment already established for the smooth mixed branch.
\end{enumerate}
Let
\[
c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}}\in \mathfrak C
\]
be a depth-$2$ readout class with the following three properties:

  \item a persistent carrier-shaped residual curvature is still present;
  \item direct carrier follow-up remains closure- and transport-compatible on the inherited branch.
\end{enumerate}
For this specific pair $(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}})$ define the local shell-admissible depth-$2$ menu by
\[
\mathcal M^{\mathrm{sm}}_2=
\mathcal M_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}})
=
\{(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}}),(\mathsf{mix},r_{\mathsf{mix}}),(\mathsf{bt},r_{\mathsf{bt}})\},
\]
where
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item $(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})$ means direct carrier-curvature follow-up on the inherited smooth mixed branch;
  \item $(\mathsf{mix},r_{\mathsf{mix}})$ means one further mixed rebalancing step without immediate carrier specialization;
  \item $(\mathsf{bt},r_{\mathsf{bt}})$ means provisional backtracking from depth $2$.
\end{enumerate}
Every fresh defect/readout-first candidate is declared off-shell in this test case because the readout class $c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}}$ carries no new local trigger of that type. This fixed data set is called the \emph{first explicit smooth-mixed depth-$2$ test case}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[First explicit third-step priority in the smooth mixed line]
\label{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-smooth-mixed-line}
Assume the first explicit smooth-mixed depth-$2$ test case of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-smooth-mixed-depth-2-test-case}. Assume in addition that the local utility scores satisfy
\[
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}};\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})
>
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}};\mathsf{mix},r_{\mathsf{mix}})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}};\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})
>
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}};\mathsf{bt},r_{\mathsf{bt}}).
\]
Then
\[
\Pi_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}})
=
\{(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})\},
\]
so that the provisional depth-$2$ continuation rule is already explicitly singleton-valued on this test case:
\[
\mathcal P^{\mathrm{prov}}_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}})
=
\{(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})\}.
\]
In particular, the smooth mixed lead path already admits one concrete third-step continuation: after bombe-first entry and boundary-offset repair first, the next move is direct carrier-curvature follow-up rather than renewed mixed hesitation or immediate backtracking.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-smooth-mixed-depth-2-test-case}, the only shell-admissible depth-$2$ siblings in the present explicit smooth-mixed case are $(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})$, $(\mathsf{mix},r_{\mathsf{mix}})$, and $(\mathsf{bt},r_{\mathsf{bt}})$. Every fresh defect/readout-first candidate is off-shell and therefore has utility $-\infty$ under Definition~\ref{def:first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-continuation-rule}. The two displayed strict inequalities then show that $(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})$ strictly dominates the only remaining admissible competitors. Hence the argmax set \(\Pi_2(h^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,c^{\mathrm{sm}}_{2,\mathrm{car}})\) is the singleton \(\{(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})\}\), which is exactly the claimed provisional depth-$2$ continuation. The last sentence is the operational reading of that singleton outcome on the inherited smooth mixed branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first explicit smooth-mixed depth-2 test case already buys]

\begin{proof}
The displayed staged path is simply the concatenation of the already stabilized depth-$0$ and depth-$1$ choices with the explicit singleton depth-$2$ outcome of Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-smooth-mixed-line}. \begin{proposition}[First explicit third-step priority in the defect/readout-near line]
\label{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-defectreadout-near-line}
Assume the first explicit defect/readout-near depth-$2$ test case of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-defectreadout-near-depth-2-test-case}. Assume in addition that the local utility scores satisfy
\[
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}};\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})
>
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}};\mathsf{mix},r^{\mathrm{dr}}_{\mathsf{mix}})
\]
and
\[
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}};\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})
>
\mathcal U_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}};\mathsf{bt},r^{\mathrm{dr}}_{\mathsf{bt}}).
\]
Then
\[
\Pi_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}})
=
\{(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})\},
\]
so that the provisional depth-$2$ continuation rule is already explicitly singleton-valued on this test case:
\[
\mathcal P^{\mathrm{prov}}_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}})
=
\{(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})\}.
\]
In particular, the defect/readout-near lead path already admits one concrete third-step continuation: after sieve-first entry and local defect/readout repair first, the next move is continued local defect/readout stabilization rather than renewed mixed hesitation or immediate backtracking.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-defectreadout-near-depth-2-test-case}, the only shell-admissible depth-$2$ siblings in the present explicit defect/readout-near case are $(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})$, $(\mathsf{mix},r^{\mathrm{dr}}_{\mathsf{mix}})$, and $(\mathsf{bt},r^{\mathrm{dr}}_{\mathsf{bt}})$. Every fresh smooth boundary-first or carrier-first candidate is off shell and therefore has utility $-\infty$ under Definition~\ref{def:first-utility-guided-provisional-depth-2-continuation-rule}. The two displayed strict inequalities then show that $(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})$ strictly dominates the only remaining admissible competitors. Hence the argmax set \(\Pi_2(h^{\mathrm{dr}}_2,c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}})\) is the singleton \(\{(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})\}\), which is exactly the claimed provisional depth-$2$ continuation. The last sentence is the operational reading of that singleton outcome on the inherited defect/readout branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first explicit defect/readout-near depth-$2$ test case already buys]
\label{cor:what-the-first-explicit-defectreadout-near-depth-2-test-case-already-buys}
On the defect/readout-near lead path, the present working line now also carries an explicit three-step staged continuation:
\[
\text{defect/readout-near optical lead}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{sieve-first defect reopening}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{local defect/readout repair first}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{continued local defect/readout stabilization}.
\]
Therefore the first currently unstabilized later depth is no longer merely manageable in the abstract on that second lead branch either; it is already concretely readable there as well. In proof terms, once the defect/readout path has reached the post-repair localized residual class \(c^{\mathrm{dr}}_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\), one may cite Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-defectreadout-near-line} and continue directly with the local stabilization move, unless a genuinely new smooth carrier/boundary drift or another off-model event forces the depth-$2$ menu to be reopened.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The displayed staged path is simply the concatenation of the already stabilized depth-$0$ and depth-$1$ choices with the explicit singleton depth-$2$ outcome of Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-defectreadout-near-line}. The final sentence is again the proof-use reading of that fact: the third step of the defect/readout-near lead branch is already fixed as long as the inherited history and readout class remain those of the present test case.
\end{proof}


\begin{remark}[Status of the first local spectral/QAM menu-operator bridge in v3.24]
\label{rem:status-of-the-first-local-spectralqam-menu-operator-bridge-in-v324}
The present v3.24.0 working line still does \emph{not} claim one global operator-theoretic resolution of the entire diagnostic tree. What it now does support, however, is one first \emph{local spectral/QAM menu-operator bridge}: finite shell-admissible continuation menus may be coded as self-adjoint local QAM operators, so that the spectral theorem recovers the same strict local priority that the utility layer already selects combinatorially.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[First QAM-coded local spectral menu operator]
\label{def:first-qam-coded-local-spectral-menu-operator}
Let $X$ be either an early-depth decision point $(d,r,c)\in \mathfrak D_\ast\times\mathfrak R\times\mathfrak C$ with utility correspondence $\Pi_\ast(d,r,c)$, or a depth-$2$ decision point $(h,c_2)\in \mathfrak H_2\times\mathfrak C$ with utility correspondence $\Pi_2(h,c_2)$. Let
\[
\mathcal M(X)
\subseteq
\mathfrak U\times\mathfrak R
\]
be the corresponding finite shell-admissible local menu, and let
\[
\mathcal H_X:=\ell^2\bigl(\mathcal M(X)\bigr)
\]
be the real Hilbert space with orthonormal basis vectors $e_m$ indexed by $m\in\mathcal M(X)$. Extend the working QAM operator-family layer by the coded operator tag
\[
\mathsf O^{\mathrm{spec}}_X:=\langle \mathsf{specmenu},X,\mathcal M(X),w_X\rangle,
\]
where the local weight function $w_X:\mathcal M(X)\to\mathbb R$ is defined by the active utility layer:
\[
w_X(m)=
\begin{cases}
\mathcal U_\ast(d,r,c;m), & \text{if } X=(d,r,c),\\[0.4em]
\mathcal U_2(h,c_2;m), & \text{if } X=(h,c_2).
\end{cases}
\]
The associated \emph{local spectral menu operator}
\[
A_X:\mathcal H_X\to\mathcal H_X
\]
is defined on basis vectors by
\[
A_X e_m = w_X(m)e_m
\qquad (m\in \mathcal M(X)).
\]
This finite diagonal self-adjoint operator, together with its QAM code $\mathsf O^{\mathrm{spec}}_X$, is called the \emph{first QAM-coded local spectral menu operator} attached to the local control point $X$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Spectral singleton readout of shell-supported local continuation]
\label{prop:spectral-singleton-readout-of-shell-supported-local-continuation}
Assume the first QAM-coded local spectral menu operator of Definition~\ref{def:first-qam-coded-local-spectral-menu-operator}. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item The operator $A_X$ is self-adjoint on the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H_X$, hence the finite-dimensional spectral theorem applies and yields an orthonormal eigenbasis together with the decomposition
  \[
  A_X=\sum_{\lambda\in\sigma(A_X)} \lambda P_\lambda.
  \]
  \item The spectrum of $A_X$ is exactly the set of utility values carried by the shell-admissible local menu:
  \[
  \sigma(A_X)=\{w_X(m):m\in \mathcal M(X)\}.
  \]
  \item If
  \[
  \lambda_{\max}=\max\sigma(A_X),
  \]
  then the top eigenspace is precisely
  \[
  E_{\max}(X)=\operatorname{span}\{e_m\,:\,m\in \Pi(X)\},
  \]
  where $\Pi(X)$ denotes the active local argmax set (namely $\Pi_\ast(d,r,c)$ or $\Pi_2(h,c_2)$ according to the type of $X$).
  \item In particular, if the active local argmax set is a singleton, say $\Pi(X)=\{m_{\max}\}$, then the top spectral projector is rank one and the unique selected continuation is recovered spectrally as
  \[
  E_{\max}(X)=\operatorname{span}\{e_{m_{\max}}\}.
  \]
\end{enumerate}
Thus the first local spectral/QAM bridge does not create a second continuation criterion. It repackages the same shell-supported local utility winner as the top eigendirection of a finite self-adjoint menu operator.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By construction, $A_X$ is diagonal in the orthonormal basis $(e_m)_{m\in\mathcal M(X)}$ with real diagonal entries $w_X(m)$. Hence $A_X$ is self-adjoint, and the finite-dimensional spectral theorem applies immediately, proving item~(i). Item~(ii) is just the standard spectrum of a diagonal operator: its eigenvalues are exactly the diagonal entries. For item~(iii), the eigenspace associated with a value $\lambda$ is the span of those basis vectors whose diagonal weight equals $\lambda$. Therefore the maximal eigenspace is the span of all basis vectors whose weights attain the maximum value, which is exactly the local argmax set returned by the active utility layer. Item~(iv) is the singleton specialization of item~(iii). The final sentence follows because the entire construction starts from the already existing shell-admissible local menu and its utility weights; the spectral operator merely rewrites the same winner in self-adjoint operator language.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first local spectral/QAM bridge already buys]
\label{cor:what-the-first-local-spectralqam-bridge-already-buys}
The present working line may now be read through one first narrow spectral/QAM control surface.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item On the smooth mixed depth-$2$ test case of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-smooth-mixed-depth-2-test-case}, if the strict utility inequalities of Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-smooth-mixed-line} hold, then the carrier-follow-up move is the unique top eigendirection of the local spectral menu operator.
  \item On the defect/readout-near depth-$2$ test case of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-defectreadout-near-depth-2-test-case}, if the strict utility inequalities of Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-defectreadout-near-line} hold, then the continued local defect/readout move is the unique top eigendirection of the local spectral menu operator.
  \item More generally, every later finite shell-admissible local menu with a strict local utility winner may be transported into the same operator language without changing its continuation choice.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the current optical control layer can already use one narrow spectral theorem input once the QAM operator layer is adapted to carry these local menu operators: the theorem does not yet solve the whole proof globally, but it does compress any finite singleton-supported local continuation into one spectral top-eigenspace statement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Items~(i) and~(ii) are the two current explicit singleton test cases combined with Proposition~\ref{prop:spectral-singleton-readout-of-shell-supported-local-continuation}. In each case, the stated strict utility inequalities identify a singleton local argmax set, so the top eigenspace of the corresponding local spectral menu operator is exactly the span of the basis vector representing the already selected continuation. Item~(iii) is the general restatement of the same proposition for any later finite shell-admissible menu. The last sentence is the proof-economy reading: once the local menu has been encoded in the adapted QAM operator layer, a singleton continuation may be cited either as a utility winner or as a spectral top-eigenspace, whichever is cleaner in the surrounding argument.
\end{proof}



\begin{remark}[Status of the first common explicit depth-$2$ continuation policy in v3.24]

Let

\{X^{\mathrm{sm}}_2,X^{\mathrm{dr}}_2\}
\subseteq
\mathfrak H_2\times\mathfrak C
\]
be the two currently explicit shell-supported depth-$2$ local control points, where

\]
is the defect/readout-near test case of Definition~\ref{def:first-explicit-defectreadout-near-depth-2-test-case}.

\]
by
\[
\kappa^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X)=
\begin{cases}

defined by

\mathcal P^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X)=

\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, one may attach to every $X\in\mathfrak X^{\mathrm{lead}}_2$ the QAM-coded policy tag
\[
\mathsf O^{\mathrm{lead}}_X:=\langle \mathsf{leaddepth2},X,\kappa^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X),\mathcal P^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X)\rangle.
\]
This classifier-driven singleton map is called the \emph{first common explicit depth-$2$ continuation policy on the leading optical regimes}.

\begin{proposition}[Agreement of the common lead-regime depth-$2$ policy with utility and spectral readout]
\label{prop:agreement-of-the-common-leadregime-depth-2-policy-with-utility-and-spectral-readout}
Assume the first common explicit depth-$2$ continuation policy of Definition~\ref{def:first-common-explicit-depth-2-continuation-policy-on-the-leading-optical-regimes}. Then for every $X\in\mathfrak X^{\mathrm{lead}}_2$ the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=(\roman*)]
  \item The policy output coincides with the already established singleton utility continuation:
  \[
  \mathcal P^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X)=\mathcal P^{\mathrm{prov}}_2(X).
  \]
  \item If $A_X$ denotes the first QAM-coded local spectral menu operator of Definition~\ref{def:first-qam-coded-local-spectral-menu-operator}, then the top eigenspace of $A_X$ is the span of the unique basis vector indexed by the element of $\mathcal P^{\mathrm{lead}}_2(X)$.
  \item In particular, the common lead-regime depth-$2$ policy introduces no new continuation criterion; it only packages the already stabilized third-step singleton outcomes into one classifier-driven rule surface.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
If $X=X^{\mathrm{sm}}_2$, then by Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-smooth-mixed-line} the provisional continuation is the singleton $\{(\mathsf{car},r_{\mathsf{car}})\}$. This is exactly the $\mathsf{sm}$ branch of Definition~\ref{def:first-common-explicit-depth-2-continuation-policy-on-the-leading-optical-regimes}. If $X=X^{\mathrm{dr}}_2$, then Proposition~\ref{prop:first-explicit-third-step-priority-in-the-defectreadout-near-line} yields the singleton $\{(\mathsf{loc},r_{\mathsf{loc}})\}$, which is exactly the $\mathsf{dr}$ branch of the same definition. This proves item~(i). Item~(ii) now follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:what-the-first-local-spectralqam-bridge-already-buys}: in each of the two explicit depth-$2$ cases, the unique utility winner is also the unique top eigendirection of the corresponding local spectral menu operator. Item~(iii) is just the operational reading of items~(i) and~(ii): the common policy does not modify the local continuation, but only gathers the two explicit singleton outcomes into one lead-type-indexed policy layer.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[What the first common explicit depth-$2$ continuation policy already buys]
\label{cor:what-the-first-common-explicit-depth-2-continuation-policy-already-buys}
The present working line now carries one first common later-depth policy window:

\begin{proof}
